Analyze every solution project: classify (.NET Framework/Core/Standard), inspect each `.csproj` TargetFramework/SDK, dependencies and graph depth. Detect `packages.config` migrations to `PackageReference`; order upgrades least-to-most dependent, isolating libraries before APIs/Azure Functions. Plan incremental upgrades, rollback checkpoints, Upgrade Assistant/manual approach, checklist and tracking dashboard.

Select TargetFramework (e.g., `net8.0`); modernize SDK/build configs, APIs, patterns (`WebHostBuilder` → `HostBuilder`), async calls, packages, shared/transitive dependencies, conflicts and migration paths. Review deprecated/removed APIs, namespaces, `Startup.cs` → `Program.cs`; consider `.NET Upgrade Assistant`, API Analyzer.

Review YAML SDK pinning; update `UseDotNet@2` and `NuGetToolInstaller`; modernize .NET 8 pipelines, CI automation, feature-branch validation builds. Validate builds, unit/integration/regression tests, logging, telemetry, connectivity, compatibility/runtime, UAT and production deployments; verify multiple repositories and final artifacts/results.

Plan branching/rollback, partial-upgrade commits, structured PRs (`Upgrade to .NET [Version]`), breaking-change tags, peer-review checklists, project documentation, release notes, stakeholder timelines, standardized workflows. Use `dotnet list package --outdated`, `dotnet migrate`, `graph.json`; generate dependency-analysis scripts/prompts and upgrade summaries.
